tyler (arch): Sharing the follow-up RFC for offline shard propagation windows — want quick takes on safety vs speed tradeoffs. gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/prop-window-rfc

sasha (eng-runtime): skimmed. this sounds like 'staged priority streaming' for big model blobs?

tyler (arch): yup. idea: send a small index first + critical shards, then background stream rest. aim to let inference start on partial model earlier.

anne (onprem): operator UX question — how do we surface 'start inference with partial set' in the operator? need a knob and a clear failure mode.

ben (sre): +1. also need metrics: percent-shards-present, stalled-shard-count, and an activation-latency gauge.

moe (sec): cryptography: when you allow partial activation we must ensure signatures still attest to the activated subset. can't accept partial without subset proofs.

tyler (arch): agreed. thinking a manifest that contains per-shard hash + signature and an activation proof that references only the subset activated. sketch:```json
{
  "manifest_version": 1,
  "shards": [
    {"id": "s1", "hash": "abc123", "priority": "high"},
    {"id": "s2", "hash": "def456", "priority": "low"}
  ],
  "signature": "sig(...)"
}
```

anne (onprem): that helps. operator could expose `activation_threshold` and `grace_window` (s). if active shards >= threshold then flip route to local inference.

sasha (eng-runtime): implementation note: KV cache indexing needs to tolerate missing layers. keep a sparse index so token-level ops don't crash when a low-priority shard is absent.

ben (sre): edge case: if a missing shard is mid-conversation and we fallback to hosted endpoint, do we stream to hosted and merge responses? that's complex.

tyler (arch): fallback merge is hard. proposal: two safe modes: degrade (return partial results with a warning) or redirect (proxy to hosted). choose per-route.

moe (sec): for signature rotation: we should avoid re-signing every partial activation. use a cheap merkle proof per shard so verification checks subset root signed by operator key.

anne (onprem): merkle sound. operator UX: include a `verify_mode` enum: STRICT (require all shards present), SUBSET_PROOF (allow subset with proofs), FORCE (operator overrides).

sasha (eng-runtime): performance: prefer streaming shards over multiple tcp connections with backpressure. single TLS session, chunked transfer with priority queue.

ben (sre): monitoring: alert when average activation_window > 30s for N clusters. also track 'stalled shard id list' to diagnose flaky disks.

tyler (arch): ops-bot — can we get an alert template for 'activation window breach' so we can plug into runbooks?

ops-bot: Created alert template: activation_window_breach. Fields: cluster, node, percent_shards, avg_window_s. Link: /alerts/activation_window_breach

moe (sec): one more threat model callout: attackers could replay old manifests with signed subset roots. include epoch and revocation list in root metadata.

anne (onprem): good catch. add `manifest_epoch` and `revocation_ptr`. operator will fetch revocation list on admin window.

sasha (eng-runtime): dev task list idea: 1) implement sparse index 2) merkle subset proof verification 3) streaming transfer with priority prefetch 4) operator flags + metrics.

ben (sre): i'll add alert and dashboards once we have metric names. also propose a canary flow: start partial activation on 10% of nodes for 24h.

tyler (arch): thanks — I'll update RFC with these action items and the merkle/subset approach. planning to land RFC next week unless objections.

moe (sec): no objections from sec, but we need a short spec for revocation/epoch semantics before landing.

anne (onprem): no objections from ops. will prep operator UX mocks.

sasha (eng-runtime): no blockers from runtime. will prototype sparse-index behavior in a branch.

ben (sre): ack, will schedule dashboards + canary playbook.
